children: Bitcoin appeared to break one of the most basic rules of time on November 7. A newly mined block showed an earlier timestamp than the block before it.
The discovery raised an unusual question: is there a bug in the Bitcoin blockchain?
Galaxy Digital research head Alex Thorn highlighted the incident, explaining why Bitcoin’s internal clock does not always follow real-world time.
Two consecutive blocks told the story.
Block 974,987: Timestamped 21:22:24 UTC.
Block 974,988: Mined afterward, but timestamped 21:19:02 UTC.
The newer block appeared more than three minutes older, according to Bitcoin’s public blockchain explorer.
Why Can Bitcoin’s Clock Run Backward?
The explanation lies in how Bitcoin mining works.
Miners choose the timestamp attached to each block. They can adjust it while searching for a valid block, creating additional combinations for their computers to test.
Bitcoin allows this flexibility under two rules:
A timestamp must exceed the median time of the previous 11 blocks.
It cannot be more than two hours ahead of a validating node’s clock.
Crucially, the timestamp does not have to be later than the immediately preceding block.

According to Thorn’s analysis, roughly 3% of Bitcoin blocks carry timestamps earlier than their parents. About one in ten arrives with a timestamp more than a minute ahead of when his node received it.
Does This Mean Bitcoin Transactions Can Be Reversed?
No. Bitcoin determines block order through cryptographic links, rather than timestamps.
Every block contains the previous block’s unique hash, establishing exactly which came first.
A genuine blockchain reorganization requires a competing chain with more accumulated mining work. Changing timestamps cannot achieve that.
However, the distinction matters for anyone relying on blockchain records to establish precisely when an event occurred.
Bitcoin’s block height establishes sequence. Its timestamp provides an approximate time.

Satoshi Nakamoto described Bitcoin as a “timestamp server” in the original whitepaper. Eighteen years later, the November 7 incident shows why that system relies on cryptographic proof rather than a perfectly accurate clock.

title: Bitcoin's Blockchain Just Ran Backward in Time. Is Something Wrong?
